en.title: Minimum Connected Blocks After Adding One Delivery Range
en.description:
Given some existing closed intervals, add exactly one closed interval [a,b] with 0≤b−a≤k. Intervals merge when they intersect or share an endpoint; integer endpoints that differ by 1 without a common point do not count as touching. Find the minimum number of connected blocks.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, and judging.
en.input: The first line contains n k (1≤n≤200000, 1≤k≤10⁹), followed by n lines of a b (1≤a≤b≤10⁹). The endpoints of the new interval can be any integers you choose.
en.explanation: Example 1: there are 4 blocks after merging; adding [5,7] of length 2 connects the first three blocks, leaving 2. Example 2: the new interval can be placed inside an existing interval, so there is still 1 block. Example 3: adding [1,5] of length 4 connects the two points into 1 block.
hints: First merge the intersecting existing intervals. One new interval can connect several consecutive blocks if and only if the left end of the last block − the right end of the first block ≤k; use two pointers to find the maximum number of blocks that can be connected.
